## Overview

Every other mediation model reports **natural** direct and indirect effects (NDE/NIE). The DAG's identification analysis states that dose is a **treatment-induced mediator–outcome confounder** of the letter-sound → reading path, so the cross-world natural effects are formally unidentified. The randomised **interventional** analogues remain well-defined in that structure because the mediator is drawn from its arm-specific distribution rather than set to the same child's incompatible natural counterfactual.

LRP78 is the interventional companion to [LRP59](../lrp-rli-med-059): the same joint mediator + outcome model ($L \to W$) and the same adjustment set, but the g-formula labels the decomposition as **interventional direct and indirect effects** (IDE/IIE).

**What the label does and does not buy** (#585 finding 2). The recanting-witness obstacle is a property of the *estimand*: an interventional contrast is well defined even when a treatment-affected variable confounds the mediator–outcome relationship, whereas a natural one is not. It is not a property of *this estimator*. Identifying an interventional effect in the presence of an exposure-induced confounder requires that confounder to be measured and integrated over — the outcome leg within its treated distribution, the mediator leg within the control one. Intervention dose is in neither, so the functional computed here identifies the interventional estimand only under the same no-exposure-induced-confounding condition the natural version needs. Read the relabelling as a change of target, not as a robustness gain, and read neither version as identified: latent general ability confounds the mediator–outcome path in both.

## Design

Same as LRP59 (phase 0, $n \approx 53$). The mediator is drawn from the fitted **covariate-conditional** law $P(M\mid C,g)$ within each covariate profile; it is not permuted across children. In this fully parametric model the natural and interventional branches therefore use the same numerical functional. LRP78's IIE and LRP59's NIE should agree up to posterior-sampling and g-formula Monte Carlo error. Agreement is an implementation check, not evidence that dose causes no distortion; a material gap would first indicate non-comparable fits or Monte Carlo error. The t3 temporal-ordering sensitivity now runs here too (#585): this is the same fitted model as LRP59 under a different label, so exempting it left the companion with less evidence than the parent whose numbers it reproduces.

## Assumptions

The interventional effects avoid the *cross-world* problem created by the treatment-induced confounder, but the mediator–outcome relationship is **still $GA$-confounded**. Moreover, dose is not represented in the fitted model, so this calculation cannot estimate or diagnose dose distortion. IDE/IIE remain **model-based adjusted decompositions** under stated assumptions — a weaker-assumption estimand class, not an identified causal route. $n \approx 53 \Rightarrow$ wide intervals.
